questionText: Consider a set-associative cache of size $2\text{ KB}$ ($1\text{ KB} = 2^{10}$ bytes) with cache block size of $64\text{ bytes}$. Assume that the cache is byte-addressable and a $32\text{-bit}$ address is used for accessing the cache. If the width of the tag field is $22\text{ bits}$, the associativity of the cache is ____________.
explanation:
Given Data:
• Cache Size = $2\text{ KB} = 2 \times 1024\text{ bytes} = 2048\text{ bytes}$
• Block Size = $64\text{ bytes} = 2^6\text{ bytes}$
• Address Size = $32\text{ bits}$
• Tag Width = $22\text{ bits}$

Step 1: Calculate Block Offset Bits
Block offset = $\log_2(64) = 6\text{ bits}$

Step 2: Calculate Set Index Bits
Address Format: $\text{Tag bits} + \text{Set Index bits} + \text{Block Offset bits} = 32\text{ bits}$
$22 + \text{Set Index bits} + 6 = 32$
$\text{Set Index bits} = 32 - (22 + 6) = 4\text{ bits}$

Step 3: Calculate Number of Sets
Number of sets = $2^4 = 16\text{ sets}$

Step 4: Calculate Total Number of Cache Lines (Blocks)
Total Lines = $\frac{\text{Cache Size}}{\text{Block Size}} = \frac{2048}{64} = 32\text{ lines}$

Step 5: Calculate Associativity ($k$)
Associativity ($k$) = $\frac{\text{Total Lines}}{\text{Number of Sets}} = \frac{32}{16} = 2$

Hence, the associativity of the cache is 2.
